description: We are a team of aspiring innovators passionate about using technology, environmental data, and machine learning to address real-world challenges. Our project, Smart Flood Monitoring and Warning System, combines NASA Earth science data, weather monitoring, and machine learning to estimate flood risk and improve environmental awareness.
summary: We developed a Smart Flood Monitoring and Warning System for Bangladesh that predicts flood risk for all 64 districts. It combines NASA IMERG satellite rainfall and NASA POWER daily weather data with a machine learning model, including one tuned for the flood-prone Haor region. A FastAPI backend and MySQL database deliver district-level risk predictions that can be turned into early warnings. The system addresses the challenge by making NASA Earth observation data practical for communities and authorities, especially where ground sensors are scarce. It matters because floods in Bangladesh repeatedly destroy homes, crops and livelihoods, and even a few extra hours of warning can save lives and reduce losses.
details: Floods repeatedly damage homes, farmland and lives, especially in low-lying regions like the Haor basin. The system collects NASA IMERG satellite rainfall data and NASA POWER daily weather data for all 64 districts, stores it in a MySQL database, and feeds it into a machine learning model trained on flood events from 2022 to 2026, including a model tuned for the Haor region. The model predicts flood risk for each district, and a FastAPI backend serves these predictions so that an early warning can reach communities, local authorities and farmers before water levels rise. The intended impact is more preparation time, fewer losses and better decisions in flood-prone areas where ground sensors are limited. We built it with Python, FastAPI, MySQL and machine learning libraries, using only open NASA data so that it is free to run and easy to reproduce. It is creative because it turns raw satellite rainfall into district-level warnings that people can act on, covering the whole country rather than a single site. Our team considered accuracy against false alarms, the limited availability of flood labels, data size, and keeping the system simple enough for non-experts to run and use.
